newsitem.title: USA: Midwest Express results hurt by fuel costs.
newsitem.headline: Midwest Express results hurt by fuel costs.

text.p: Midwest Express Holdings Inc said its fourth quarter and 1996 results were hurt by higher fuel prices.
The rise in jet fuel prices hurt operating income by $3.0 million or $0.30 a share in the fourth quarter and $8.9 million or $0.86 a share for the year, the airline said.
For the fourth quarter, fuel prices rose about $0.189 per gallon or 27.5 percent from a year earlier and for the full year, fuel prices rose $0.148 per gallon or 23.7 percent.

The company's fourth quarter cost per available seat mile increased 5.2 percent from the fourth quarter of 1995 and full-year costs were up 8.9 percent -- primarily the result of the increased fuel costs and the company's new profit sharing program.

Midwest posted fourth quarter earnings of $3.9 million or $0.62 a share on total operating revenues of $78.1 million, compared with earnings of $2.9 million or $0.46 a share on operating revenues of $63.4 million.
